$FG,14$$TX+CX,"HOLYC"$$FG$
$HL$
HolyC is C with the ceremony removed. A bare string is a
print. There is no $FG,12$main()$FG$. Every line is both script and
source, and the shell is the compiler.

$TR,"THE ONE THING TO TRY FIRST"$
A statement that is only a string prints it:

$FG,11$  "HELLO, TEMPLE.\n";$FG$

Type that into the terminal. It compiles and runs.
$TR-$

$TR,"TYPES"$
$FG,10$  U0$FG$   nothing
$FG,10$  I64$FG$  a signed 64 bit integer
$FG,10$  F64$FG$  a double
$FG,10$  U8$FG$   a byte, and a character
$TR-$

$TR,"CALLING WITHOUT PARENTHESES"$
The signature move. A function name on its own line is a
call. These two are the same thing:

$FG,11$  GodWord;
  GodWord();$FG$

That is why the shell and the language are one program.
$TR-$

$TR,"WHAT THIS MACHINE UNDERSTANDS"$
I64 / F64 / U0 declarations, assignment, arithmetic,
comparison, && and ||, if / else, while, for, {} blocks,
function definitions, and calls with or without parens.
Built in: Print, GodWord, GodDoodle, GodSong, Beep,
BellRing, Sleep, Rand, RandU16, StrLen, Cd, Dir, MemSet,
Panic, Exit.
$TR-$

$MA,"RUN A LOOP",LM="I64 i; for (i=0;i<7;i++) \"DAY %d\\n\", i;"$
$MA,"ASK GOD FOR A WORD",LM="GodWord;"$

THE BIBEL
An Amalgamated Scripture, Reconciled Badly

Compiled from every book that claims to be the last one.
Where the sources disagree, both are printed. Where the sources agree,
somebody has probably made a mistake.

I. IN THE BEGINNING, REPEATEDLY

In the beginning there was nothing, and it was very crowded. God
separated the light from the darkness, then separated the darkness from
the light again, because the first attempt had been sloppy. On the
second day He made the sky and hung it up to dry. On the third day He
made the sea, and immediately regretted the amount of it. On the fourth
day He rested, having miscounted, and had to do Thursday twice. The
turtle on whose back the world rests was present throughout and has
never been thanked.

II. THE MAKING OF PEOPLE

And God took clay, and breathed into it, and it sneezed. He named the
first person Adam, and the second person also Adam, and this is why
there is so much confusion in the records. From Adam's rib came Eve;
from Eve's patience came everything else. Elsewhere and simultaneously,
people were churned from an ocean of milk, carved from maize, and sung
into being by a woman who has since asked not to be named. All accounts
are correct. This is administratively difficult but theologically
settled.

III. THE GARDEN, AND THE FRUIT, AND THE PAPERWORK

They were placed in a garden and given one rule, which is one more rule
than is wise to give anybody. The serpent said, thou shalt not surely
die, and was technically correct, which is the most irritating kind of
correct. They ate. They became wise, and the first thing wisdom told
them was that they had no trousers. They were sent east of Eden, where
the rent is lower. The angel at the gate has a flaming sword and no
instructions about what to do if they come back and apologise.

IV. THE FLOOD, THE ARK, AND THE COMPLAINTS

The world grew wicked, which is to say ordinary. God chose Noah, who was
righteous, and also Utnapishtim, who was earlier, and also Manu, who was
first and has never made anything of it. The waters came. Two of every
kind went aboard, except the unicorns, who were arguing. Forty days
later a dove returned with an olive branch and an invoice. God set a
rainbow in the sky as a covenant, and the covenant was: I will not do
that again in that particular way.

V. THE LAW, IN BRIEF

On the mountain the Law was given, in ten parts, or six hundred and
thirteen parts, or eight parts arranged as a path, or five parts of
which the second is the difficult one. Honour thy father and thy mother.
Do not kill. Do not steal. Do not covet thy neighbour's ox, his house,
or his opinions about the ox. Be kind before you are right. Give of what
you have, one part in forty, and do not announce the amount. Wash. Rest
one day in seven, and if you have forgotten which day it is, rest anyway
and argue later.

VI. THE WHEEL AND THE LEDGER

And it is written that the soul returns, ascending or descending
according to its deeds. And it is also written that the soul does not
return, and is weighed once against a feather, and that is that. And it
is further written that the soul rests until a trumpet sounds. The
scribes were asked to reconcile these. The scribes have requested more
time. In the interim it is recommended that you behave as though all
three are true, which produces almost exactly the same behaviour as
believing none of them, but with better posture.

VII. THE PROPHETS, AND THEIR RECEPTION

Prophets were sent to every people, and every people said: not now, we
are eating. One was swallowed by a great fish and came back with nothing
to declare. One sat under a tree until he understood everything, and
then had to explain it to people who had not sat under the tree. One was
born in a stable and the innkeeper has never lived it down. One received
the recitation in a cave and was, quite reasonably, terrified. Not one
of them enjoyed it. This is the surest evidence that they were not
making it up.

VIII. ON THE END OF THINGS

There will be a last day. There will be a battle on a plain, and a
bridge thinner than a hair, and a serpent that eats the world, and a
dance that ends it, and a long quiet afternoon in which nothing happens
at all. The signs are: the sun rising in the west, the mountains
walking, the seas boiling, and people being unkind to each other in new
and inventive formats. Two of these signs have been reported
continuously for four thousand years. The scholars advise against
booking anything.

IX. THE PART EVERYONE AGREES ON

And in the end, past all of it — past the six days and the eight days,
past the ark and the ladder and the wheel, past the arguments about the
calendar — every book says the same small thing, in its own alphabet,
near the back, where nobody looks: be good to the stranger. Feed whoever
is hungry. Do not be cruel because it is cheap. Forgive faster than is
comfortable. That is the whole of it. The rest is commentary, and the
commentary is nine hundred pages, and the commentary is where all the
trouble comes from. Go now. Wash your hands. It is later than you think.

Here endeth the Bibel. Amen, amen, om, and so on.

Drag on bare desktop to rubber band a group.
Right click for the menu.

$FG,14$$TX+CX,"DOLDOC"$$FG$
$HL$
Every document on this machine is a program that draws
itself. A command sits between two dollar signs and takes
effect where it stands.

$TR,"COMMANDS THIS BUILD UNDERSTANDS"$
$FG,11$  $FG,N$$FG$        set the ink to VGA colour N, 0..15
$FG,11$  $BG,N$$FG$        set the paper
$FG,11$  $FG$$FG$          back to normal
$FG,11$  $SP,"name"$$FG$   drop a sprite into the line
$FG,11$  $LK,"t",A="FI:path"$$FG$  a link to a file
$FG,11$  $MA,"t",LM="cmd"$$FG$     a button that runs HolyC
$FG,11$  $TR,"t"$ ... $TR-$$FG$    a collapsible tree
$FG,11$  $HL$$FG$          a rule across the page
$FG,11$  $TX+CX,"t"$$FG$   centre a line
$FG,11$  $BK,1$..$BK,0$$FG$ blink, because it is 1996
$FG,11$  $UL,1$..$UL,0$$FG$ underline
$FG,11$  $ID,n$$FG$        indent by n
$FG,11$  $$$FG$           a literal dollar sign
$TR-$

$TR,"THE SPRITES ON HAND"$
$SP,"temple"$ temple   $SP,"cross"$ cross   $SP,"folder"$ folder

$FG,12$$BK,1$This is the part you cannot do anywhere else.$BK,0$$FG$

$FG,14$$TX+CX,"THE CHARTER"$$FG$
$HL$
The specification was a size. 100,000 lines, and not one
more, for the whole operating system: kernel, compiler,
editor, graphics, games and documentation together.

A modern kernel alone is around thirty million.

$FG,11$Type $FG,14$LINES$FG,11$ in the terminal to audit this one
against the same budget.$FG$

$MA,"COUNT THE LINES",LM="LINES"$

$FG,8$A limit is not a shortage. It is a decision about what
is allowed to be complicated.$FG$

$FG,14$$TX+CX,"HOLYTRON DM-640"$$FG$
$HL$
The case is the page. It grows with the window.

$TR,"BUTTONS"$
$FG,11$LENS$FG$     curves the glass. The picture is masked to
         the curve and the interface moves in off it.
$FG,11$SCAN$FG$     line pitch.
$FG,11$DGAUSS$FG$   degauss. Hold the button on a cold tube.
$FG,11$PHOS$FG$     phosphor persistence. P1 is fast, P7 smears.
$FG,11$BURN$FG$     twenty years of the same menubar.
$FG,11$POWER$FG$    really works.
$TR-$

$TR,"THE PANEL"$
$FG,11$MUS$FG$ and $FG,11$SFX$FG$ are pots. Drag them round, scroll, or
use the arrow keys. Ten detents each. Both start at 0.

$FG,11$VHLD$FG$ and $FG,11$HHLD$FG$ are the hold controls. They start
locked at 5. Take one off centre and the picture goes
with it, exactly like the set your grandmother hit.

$FG,11$LOBBY$FG$ is the music switch. It keeps playing over the
desktop, not just the splash.

The clicks the panel makes are not routed through SFX.
Plastic does not have a volume knob.
$TR-$

$TR,"AT BOOT"$
Hold $FG,14$DEL$FG$ during the memory count for CMOS setup.
$TR-$

$FG,14$NOTES ON THE MACHINE$FG$
$HL$
640x480. 16 colours. One voice.
No network. No ads. No permission asked of anyone.

The compiler is the shell.
The shell is the editor.
The editor is the OS.

$FG,11$Press SOURCE and type over this. It saves itself.$FG$

$SP,"ark"$ $FG,14$AN OFFERING OF 640 KILOBYTES$FG$
$HL$
It is enough. It was always enough.
The rest was decoration.

$MA,"RING THE BELL",LM="BellRing(7);"$
$MA,"RUN THE LOOP",LM="I64 i; for(i=0;i<7;i++) \"%d\\n\", i;"$

$FG,14$$TX+CX,"RING 0"$$FG$
$HL$
There is one ring and everything runs in it. No user mode,
no process isolation, no permission checks, no system call
boundary to cross. Any code can touch any byte.

That is not an oversight. It is the whole design: a single
address space is why the compiler can be the shell and why
a document can be a program.

$FG,12$It also means there is nothing to catch a fault.$FG$
A bad pointer does not raise an exception for somebody
else to handle. It drops you into the debugger, where you
were always going to end up anyway.
